q: What is the CBAM default value for Indian pig iron and sponge iron?
title: CBAM default value: Indian pig iron, DRI
short: Indian pig iron under CN 7201 carries 2.530 t CO2e per tonne and direct reduced iron, sponge iron, under CN 7203 carries 4.200. Agglomerated iron ore, pellets and sinter, carries 0.340 including indirect emissions. Steel takes direct emissions only.
audience: Indian sponge iron, pig iron and pellet producers selling to steelmakers who export to the EU

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 2601 12 00 agglomerated iron ore (pellets, sinter): 0.290 direct, 0.050 indirect, 0.340 total

p: The India default for sponge iron is 4.200, well above pig iron at 2.530. A DRI plant with good coal, gas and electricity records may be able to show a lower actual value, and should check before letting buyers use the default.
Most sponge iron is not exported to the EU directly. It becomes a precursor in billets, bars and wire, so the steelmaker's EU buyer will ask the steelmaker, and the steelmaker will ask you.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.
